passages.note: House Third Reading roll call naming her vote and the divided tally; the page prints no provision text.

passages.provision_quote: Except for a form produced by the United States election assistance commission, any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Chaptered text of the bill she voted on; it prints the operative registration provision but names no voter.
Bill-status page fixing the instrument and its enactment; Pingerelli is not among the listed sponsors, so it shows no act of hers.

rows.reasoning: Pingerelli voted Y on House Third Reading of HB2492 (2022), a single-subject registration bill whose operative section provides that "any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F" and that the recorder "shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship." That is the rung "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote." The tally, "Passed 31-26-3-0-0," is far from near-unanimous, and the 2022 act falls in an earlier term in the same chamber of this legislature (V5 option B).
